record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Function Field Arithmetic — The Influence of John Tate’s Work
record.context_brief: Functional equation for Goss zeta values
record.original_question: For the Goss zeta function over A = Fq[t], whose interpolation includes both positive and negative integers, what functional equation should connect the special values at positive integers to the special values at negative integers, and how should the function-field gamma factors enter as the factor at infinity in such a functional equation?

evidence.quote: David Goss (see [Gos96]) interpolated the zeta values at positive integers above to a much larger continuous space containing, in particular, the negative integers.

But still no functional equation connecting the two sets of values is understood in contrast to the Riemann zeta function functional equation whose nice analysis was done in Tate’s thesis. We do have good analogs [Tha04] of Gamma functions, but do not understand them as a factor at infinity for zeta as in Tate’s thesis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, set $A = \mathbb{F}_q[t]$, let $K = \mathbb{F}_q(t)$, let $K_\infty = \mathbb{F}_q((1/t))$ be the completion at the infinite place, and let $\mathbb{C}_\infty$ be the completion of an algebraic closure of $K_\infty$. For a positive integer $s$, define the Goss zeta value
$$\zeta_A(s) \;=\; \sum_{\substack{a \in A \\ a \text{ monic}}} \frac{1}{a^s} \;\in\; K_\infty.$$
Goss extended this construction to a continuous interpolation $\zeta_A : S_\infty \to \mathbb{C}_\infty$, where $S_\infty = \mathbb{C}_\infty^\times \times \mathbb{Z}_p$ is the Goss "complex plane", whose domain contains both the positive integers and the negative integers (so that the special values $\zeta_A(-n)$ for $n \geq 0$ are defined, and in fact lie in $A$). For each integer $n \geq 0$ one also has function-field gamma factors $\Gamma(n+1)$ constructed in the theory of $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear (arithmetic and geometric) gamma functions on $A$.
 
Problem. Formulate and establish a functional equation, in the style of Tate's thesis, that relates the family of special values $\{\zeta_A(s)\}_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}}$ to the family of special values $\{\zeta_A(-n)\}_{n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}}$ of the Goss zeta function for $A = \mathbb{F}_q[t]$. The functional equation should incorporate the function-field gamma functions as the local factor at the infinite place of $K$, in analogy with the role played by $\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$ in the classical functional equation of the Riemann zeta function.
artifact.category_tag: Goss zeta function and function field arithmetic
artifact.status_search_result: No functional equation in the style of Tate's thesis is known relating the Goss zeta values at positive integers to those at negative integers for $A=\mathbb{F}_q[t]$, nor is there an established role for the function-field gamma functions as the factor at infinity. Recent work focuses on zeros and the Riemann-hypothesis analogue (Sheats 1998 and successors), but the desired functional equation remains unestablished.

status_evidence.title: Goss zeta function - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Goss zeta function is an equicharacteristic analogue of the Riemann zeta function; Sheats (1998) proved an analogue of the Riemann hypothesis. No analogue of the classical functional equation is stated.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references describe interpolation to negative integers and the Riemann-hypothesis analogue but not a Tate-style functional equation.

status_evidence.title: Zeros of the Goss zeta function
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2023) study of zeros of the Goss zeta function; investigates negative integer values but does not provide a Tate-thesis-style functional equation with a gamma factor at infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Current research on the Goss zeta function continues to study its values and zeros, with no known Tate-style functional equation.
